summary: Warwick Light has guided ships through the narrow water off Warwick Neck since 1826; its 1932 cast-iron tower was moved 50 feet after the 1938 hurricane.

corrections.why: The tower standing today was built in 1932 (nomination; archive). The 1826-27 light was torn down in 1932, so the record's 1827 belongs to the first tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination says the light was established in 1826 and the wooden tower on the dwelling was completed the following year (1827). LighthouseFriends says the station was completed in 1826, and the archive gives 1827 as the establishment year. The record's 1826 first_lit and 1827 built are kept as the sources give them.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved conflicts left in the story: (1) the first tower is 18 ft (nomination) or 30 ft of stone (LighthouseFriends); (2) the surviving keeper's dwelling is dated 1889 (appropriation, archive, LighthouseFriends) and 1899 (nomination); (3) the present tower is 51 ft cast iron (nomination), 31 ft steel (LighthouseFriends), 28 ft base to lantern (archive) and cast iron, erected 1889 (GSA invitation for bids, which conflicts with the nomination and LighthouseFriends); (4) the light is 51 ft above sea level (nomination) and 54 ft above water (archive); the record's focal height of 20.1 m and range of 10.0 nm come from ENC and are not supported by the sources read, so they are not in facts; the nomination's 12 miles is probably statute miles (about 10.4 nm); (5) the strait is a half mile (nomination) or three-quarters (LighthouseFriends) wide; (6) automation: the archive says 1985 and LighthouseFriends says a modern lens replaced the Fresnel lens that year, while the nomination (which led to the 1988 listing) describes a keeper on the grounds and automation by 1990. The GSA invitation is dated 18 June 2026 and says bids will be received continuously; the sources read do not say how the sale ended. The LighthouseFriends date for the 1939 move is inland, the nomination says north. The keeper roster was matched by name and position to USLHS Warwick Neck (0.9 km from the OSM point); roster lines are as the archive prints them and are not checked against the NARA registers. Jorgen Bakken's Shinnecock link is LighthouseFriends' statement only; the corpus has two Shinnecock records, so no other_stations link is made. Nathaniel Dodge carries one archive slug across Warwick Neck (1898, 1905) and Poplar Point (1885-1893); the archive joins them, the story does not. A Chronicling America search (Warwick Neck, Bakken, RI, 1912-1932) returned no hits, so no newspaper evidence is used. The Lighthouse Board volume for 1896-97 gives the 250-ft fence in a list without a scan page that could be confirmed, so that report is not cited; the 1896 fence figure rests on the nomination. The 1901 Board volume is catalogued by year only (its title page is generic), so it is cited as the 1901 volume. NRHP page numbers are read from the 'Page' labels in each continuation-sheet header. The Rhode Island photo lacks a licence and is not added.
